name: OFFSET
description: OFFSET returns a reference that is a specified number of rows and columns from a starting cell or range.
tldr: Returns a range shifted by a given number of rows and columns from a starting point.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Number of rows to shift down (positive) or up (negative).

parameters.name: cols
parameters.description: Number of columns to shift right (positive) or left (negative).

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Height of the returned range in rows (optional).

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Width of the returned range in columns (optional).

basicExample.description: Return the value one row below A1
basicExample.explanation: Starts at A1 and shifts down 1 row, returning A2.

advancedExamples.title: Dynamic range
advancedExamples.description: Create a range that grows as data is added
advancedExamples.result: Average of all populated cells in column A
advancedExamples.explanation: COUNTA determines the height of the range dynamically.

advancedExamples.title: 2D offset
advancedExamples.description: Return a 3x2 range starting 2 rows down and 1 column right from A1
advancedExamples.explanation: OFFSET returns a 3-row by 2-column range starting at B3.

howItWorks: OFFSET starts at the reference and moves the specified number of rows and columns. It then optionally expands the result to a range of the given height and width. It returns a reference, not a value, so it is typically used inside another function.

howToSteps.name: Choose starting cell
howToSteps.text: Select the anchor cell or range.

howToSteps.name: Specify row offset
howToSteps.text: Enter how many rows to move down (positive) or up (negative).

howToSteps.name: Specify column offset
howToSteps.text: Enter how many columns to move right (positive) or left (negative).

howToSteps.name: Optional size
howToSteps.text: Set height and width to return a range larger than one cell.

limitations: Volatile: recalculates on every workbook change, which can slow performance.
Can be hard to debug because the returned range is not visible.
Does not work across closed workbooks.
Using it with entire-column references can cause performance issues.

commonErrors.cause: The offset points outside the worksheet boundaries.
commonErrors.fix: Reduce the row or column offset values.

commonErrors.cause: OFFSET is volatile and used in many cells.
commonErrors.fix: Use INDEX or structured references instead where possible.

commonErrors.cause: Height or width parameters are incorrect.
commonErrors.fix: Double-check the height and width values.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: OFFSET works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between OFFSET and INDEX?
faq.answer: OFFSET returns a reference by shifting from a starting point. INDEX returns a value or reference at a specific position in an array.

faq.question: Is OFFSET volatile?
faq.answer: Yes, it recalculates whenever the sheet changes.

faq.question: Can I use OFFSET for dynamic named ranges?
faq.answer: Yes, but modern Excel often prefers structured tables or FILTER.
